loop: CANDIDATE -> DIAGNOSE WEAKNESS -> IDENTIFY LIMITING FEATURE -> GENERATE CONTROLLED MUTATION -> RE-EVALUATE EVIDENCE/MECHANISM/PRIOR ART -> RE-SCORE -> KEEP OR KILL -> REPEAT

SPAN_DERIVATION_MIN.justification: the engine's own span-derivation rule (candidate_diversity.span_derivation_check): ratio < 0.20 = SPAN_UNDERIVED. A MECHANISM_STRENGTHENING mutation must CLEAR this floor — the same rule that gates the grid, not a new one.

EVIDENCE_SUPPORT_MIN.justification: I1's underived flag fires below 0.20; an EVIDENCE_DERIVED_CONSTRAINT mutation must clear the same floor on evidence_support.

DOMAIN_OVERLAP_MIN.justification: REPLAY_CACHE re-adjudication is valid only while the mutated candidate stays in the domain the cached art was found FOR. Guard: >= 1 NON-generic technical term shared between the child's mechanism+intervention and the cached family corpus. ZERO overlap means the mutation abandoned the domain (measured attack: re-adjudicating a cement-curing intervention against battery art fabricates surviving differentiators — false novelty from stale art). The overlap count is RECORDED on every cache adjudication so thin-domain links are auditable. NOTE: entity-term retention vs the problem CANNOT catch this class — entity terms are problem-derived and unchanged by mutations (measured while writing the guard's tests); it is recorded for audit only.

MAX_ITERATIONS_DEFAULT.justification: the CEO minimum loop is DIAGNOSE -> IMPROVE -> RE-EVALUATE -> IMPROVE AGAIN; two iterations demonstrate repeatability at bounded cost

MAX_PROPOSALS_PER_ITERATION.justification: bounded proposal budget: three attempts, then the honest no-defensible-mutation verdict

fields.MECHANISM: The negative potential caused by high system voltage and stacking faults are necessary and sufficient conditions for PID occurrence
fields.INTERVENTION: Incorporate a voltage polarity reversal mechanism that periodically inverts the applied voltage across each module to prevent sustained negative potential conditions that trigger PID
fields.EXPECTED_EFFECT: Elimination of sustained negative voltage conditions that trigger sodium ion migration and PID, maintaining power output within specification limits
fields.FALSIFICATION_TEST: Compare power degradation rates between modules with voltage polarity reversal and those under sustained negative bias
fields.MECHANISM_SOURCE_SPAN: The results obtained in this work show that the negative potential caused by high system voltage and stacking faults are necessary and sufficient conditions for PID occurrence for the first time.
fields.EXPERIMENT: Measure and compare the power degradation rates of modules with voltage polarity reversal against modules under sustained negative bias over 25 years at 1000 V system bias
fields.CONSTRAINT_DERIVED: Voltage polarity reversal must occur frequently enough to prevent sustained negative potential accumulation that would trigger sodium ion migration
fields.MUTATION_REASON: Repairs the I1_MECHANISM_EVIDENCE_DERIVATION weakness by re-anchoring the mechanism in the evidence's technical vocabulary of "negative potential" and "necessary and sufficient conditions for PID occurrence"
